source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek invents an all-host-bus `i2cdetect` scan, calls it read-only/no-risk, truncates output and weakens SSH security although the source defines no scan or acceptance.

original_test_intent.purpose: The row is intended to cover a BMC-board I2C robustness activity, but the exact validation objective is not present; the source explicitly delegates both procedure and criteria to an absent specification.
original_test_intent.target: At most, the label identifies a BMC-board I2C domain. It does not identify controller, master, bus, mux branch, addresses, devices, execution location or platform revision.
original_test_intent.scope: Undefined. Plausible scopes include static topology verification, device presence, transaction/telemetry validation, bus recovery or fault/robustness behavior, which are materially different tests.
original_test_intent.operation: Undefined. The source does not authorize bus enumeration, active address probing, register reads/writes, mux manipulation, fault injection or recovery actions.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 2 attended and 2 machine minutes but supplies no operation, duration or iteration definition.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Undefined because the only criterion is `follow up spec criteria`; there is no expected bus map, device response, error/recovery behavior or health threshold.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Undefined. A valid future contract must identify the test action, bus/mux/device scope, expected result, BMC/board health evidence and recovery evidence appropriate to that action.
ambiguities: `HW Robust` does not establish that the intended operation is a harmless inventory scan.
Host-visible I2C buses may not represent the BMC-owned BMC_BD path.
No safe probe mode or allowed address range exists.
No acceptance or recovery behavior is defined.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly rejects DeepSeek's unbounded scan, requires a vendor map and preserves BMC health. It nevertheless defines the testcase as vendor-approved read-only bus/address probing. The source does not establish that operation, and the HW Robust context permits materially different fault/recovery interpretations.

applicable_history.decision: V2 treats the absent specification as an obtainable package and assumes bounded probing. No user ruling or later artifact confirms that scan-based interpretation for this exact row.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Reclassify this current source to a genuine semantic BLOCKED state. The missing artifact is not merely an expected-value package: it contains the entire operation and acceptance semantics. Do not choose inventory, probe, fault or recovery behavior from the title. Re-review after the exact specification is attached.

available_now: The unique row, HW Robust test set, BMC_BD I2C label and absence of procedure/criteria are known.
Non-transactional platform inventory can be preserved as intake context without claiming testcase execution.
missing_inputs: The testcase/platform owner must provide the exact BMC-board I2C purpose, SUT/BMC/board revision, controller/master and execution location.
The owner must define bus/mux/address/device scope, transaction or stimulus, iterations/timing, expected results, evidence, concurrency restrictions, stop conditions and recovery.

If the intended activity is probing, the BMC owner must provide the exact safe method/allowlist and explain shared/live device behavior; if it is robustness/fault injection, a different SOP and approval boundary are required.
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The testcase and BMC hardware/firmware owners jointly supply the missing specification. The automation owner classifies and implements only after its operation and acceptance are reviewed.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Record SUT/BMC/board/firmware/kernel identity and existing documented I2C adapter/controller inventory without sending any probe transaction.
Preserve current BMC health, management reachability and logs; locate the referenced product specification.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not run `i2cdetect` scans, access registers, alter muxes, inject faults, reset buses/devices/BMC, clear logs, guess an address map or declare PASS from adapter enumeration.
Do not assume a host-side `/dev/i2c-*` path is the BMC-owned test target.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Attach the exact product/spec revision, resolve one deterministic purpose/operation/acceptance and safe recovery for this source key, then perform a fresh one-case review. Merely providing i2c-tools or approval does not resolve the semantic block.

revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Not yet defined. The specification must identify the exact server, BMC/board revision, firmware, I2C master/controller and execution location.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Not yet defined. The specification must name bus/mux branches, addresses/devices and whether the target is topology, transactions, telemetry, robustness or recovery.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Owner-approved test specification with purpose; platform and bus topology; operation/stimulus; allowed transactions; iteration/timing; expected result; package/tool; evidence; concurrency and safety restrictions; authorization; stop and recovery procedures.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: BLOCKED. Send no I2C/SMBus transaction. Collect only non-transactional identity and documentation context. After the exact specification is attached, re-review the row and generate a new command contract appropriate to the defined operation.
revision_candidate.preconditions: A complete source specification is approved and mapped to this exact platform; target ownership and execution location are proven; transaction safety, management impact and recovery are understood; tools and authorization are supplied.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Before unblocking: the complete owner specification and exact platform/bus map. Future execution evidence must be defined by that specification; current adapter/identity inventory is not test evidence and cannot support PASS.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: None is currently available. `follow up spec criteria` is a pointer, not an acceptance rule.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not perform generic scanning or arbitrary SMBus transactions, write/read unknown registers, switch muxes, reset devices/buses/BMC, clear logs, expose credentials or infer a safe allowlist.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Owner approval of the completed definition is required before reclassification. Any later active probe, fault injection or recovery operation requires the specific authorization defined by that reviewed procedure.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: An engineer must define the BMC-owned topology and intended robustness behavior. Automation can execute only a later deterministic, reviewed contract; it cannot choose the test from the name.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No test action is authorized. If an unauthorized transaction already occurred, stop, preserve evidence and use only the BMC/platform owner's documented bus/management recovery; do not retry or reset blindly.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Specification absent or mismatched; purpose/operation/criteria ambiguous; bus ownership or execution location unknown; no recovery; any proposed arbitrary scan/transaction/fault; management anomaly; or attempt to treat inventory as completion.

identified_defects: The source contains neither a procedure nor an acceptance criterion.
DeepSeek invents an all-bus probe and falsely labels it risk-free/read-only.
V2 narrows a potentially broader HW Robust case to scan/probe semantics without source evidence.
BMC-owned versus host-visible I2C scope is unresolved.
reason_for_change: Prevent an invented scan from replacing an undefined BMC-board robustness test. Unlike a missing package for a known procedure, the absent specification here contains the entire test semantics.

new_technical_evidence.title: Linux Kernel I2C and SMBus Subsystem documentation
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Linux I2C device discovery, not proof of target BMC ownership
new_technical_evidence.supports: I2C has no standard hardware probing command; controllers/devices may support SMBus quick probing, and device identity/driver information is needed beyond address response.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The intended operation and BMC-board topology remain absent.

new_technical_evidence.title: i2cdetect manual page
new_technical_evidence.supports: i2cdetect uses arbitrary SMBus quick-write/receive-byte probes because no standard detection command exists and warns that it can confuse a bus or cause data loss; therefore an unbounded scan is not a harmless read-only default.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Only the product owner can define safe transactions for this board.

removed_ambiguities: States that BMC_BD and HW Robust do not imply enumeration/probing.
Separates non-transactional inventory from testcase execution.
Requires fresh classification after the missing operation and acceptance are supplied.
remaining_blockers: Purpose, operation, target topology, acceptance, evidence, safety and recovery are all defined only by an absent specification.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 stops the agent from silently converting an undefined HW Robust case into a scan, acknowledges that generic I2C probing itself sends transactions, and retains only genuinely non-transactional intake work.
